name: Bluish Grey-Green
lede: Bluish Grey-Green is a bluish shade of [[grey-green|grey-green]], one of Robert Ridgway's working names built by the plain grammar of modifier plus base color.

sections.title: A modifier, not a new color
sections.body: Bluish Grey-Green joins the modifier *bluish* to the base color [[grey-green]], itself a compound of two basic hue words [1][4]. Ridgway's 1912 plate XLII, hue 41-triple-prime, sets it at lightness 61 and a low-to-moderate chroma of 14 [1][4]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the matching block, 149, 'pale green,' a Delta-E of 5.3 from Ridgway's point [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[greyish-teal]], [[medici-blue]] and [[grey-celadon]], at 4, 4.6 and 4.7 ΔE [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 0.95% of 23,781 paintings, 226 paintings; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 117 of them [3]. That ranks it more common than 61% of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 1.4% of that century's 1,674 paintings, 3.0 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, by lightness rank, in 38% of its 117 appearances [3]. Claude Monet paints it most often by count, 4 of his 50 works here, 8% of them, but no painter stands out against the museum baseline for it[3]. The earliest dated appearance is a 1400 painting by the Master of Rubielos de Mora, 512 years before the name's first documented record in 1912; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3].

questions.q: Which two basic hue words combine to form the base color behind Bluish Grey-Green?
True or false: unlike most names in this batch, no painter in our archive stands out from the museum baseline for Bluish Grey-Green.
Which Ridgway plate and hue number does Bluish Grey-Green share with Dark Bluish Grey-Green?

openers: Bluish Grey-Green and Dark Bluish Grey-Green share the exact same Ridgway plate and hue, differing only in tone.
No painter in our archive stands out for it.
